# Moses Yebei - repository estate

> 1521 public repositories, analysed and related to each other.
> Provenance is stated per fact rather than claimed for the site as a whole.
> The file census, architecture pass, dependency scan, advisory scan, hygiene
> audit, domain classification and eight-category grade are EXTRACTED: measured
> from a tree, a history or a manifest, reproducible from the same inputs, no
> model involved. The semantic similarity edges are INFERRED: cosine distance
> between neural embeddings (nvidia/nv-embedqa-e5-v5) of a text built from each
> repository description, topics and generated summary. Treat them as a strong
> hint, not as a measurement. Every edge in the relation layer carries which of
> the two it is. Repositories that have not been analysed are marked as such
> rather than being reported as clean.

## Data

- [Schema](https://moses-y.github.io/data/schema.json): what every field in the index means. Read this first; the record keys are single letters.
- [Index](https://moses-y.github.io/data/index.json): all 1521 repositories with language, domain, kind, capabilities, hygiene severities and semantic coordinates, plus 3444 similarity edges. Large - prefer the neighbourhood files below for traversal.
- [Relations manifest](https://moses-y.github.io/data/relations.json): edge types, thresholds and counts for the relation layer.
- [Clusters](https://moses-y.github.io/data/clusters.json): 61 groups of near-duplicate work covering 167 repositories, each with member grades and which one is the keeper.
- [Cluster report](https://moses-y.github.io/data/clusters.md): the same 61 groups written out as prose, cross-domain ones first, each with its keeper and how much of it is unaudited. Read this instead of clusters.json if you want the argument rather than the records.
- [Neighbourhood](https://moses-y.github.io/data/kin/1004131322.json): one file per repository id, about 1 KB each: nearest semantic kin and repositories sharing its dependency stack, with the shared packages named. Fetch https://moses-y.github.io/data/kin/<id>.json to walk from one repository to its neighbours without loading the index.
- [Grades](https://moses-y.github.io/data/grades.json): 1518 graded repositories, mean 60.6, with the per-category score, weight and the findings charged against each.
- [Hygiene](https://moses-y.github.io/data/hygiene.json): the raw audit findings behind the grades.
- [Dependencies](https://moses-y.github.io/data/deps.json): declared dependencies per repository by ecosystem.
- [Search](https://moses-y.github.io/data/search.json): inverted index, token to position in the index records.

## Answering a question with these files

1. Resolve a repository to its numeric id once, from /data/index.json or /data/search.json. Ids are stable across renames.
2. Fetch https://moses-y.github.io/data/kin/<id>.json, about 1 KB. It carries both edge types with their provenance, so "what else is like this" costs one small request rather than a parse of the 1139 KB index.
3. Repeat step 2 for any neighbour id. Traversal never needs the index again.
4. For a group rather than a neighbour, /data/clusters.json names the keeper; /data/clusters.md is the same thing as prose.

Prefer a neighbour that appears in both the stack and semantic lists of a kin file: the extracted edge corroborates the inferred one, which is the strongest signal here that a repository is a usable starting point.

## Pages

- [Projects](https://moses-y.github.io/projects.html): every repository with its measured facts.
- [Code Graph](https://moses-y.github.io/knowledge-graph.html): the semantic map, similarity edges drawn.
- [Code Brain](https://moses-y.github.io/code-brain.html): domains to languages to repositories to modules.
- [Briefings](https://moses-y.github.io/blog/): a written analysis per repository at /blog/<name>.html.
- [Site map](https://moses-y.github.io/sitemap.html): everything, grouped by domain.

## Notes

- Domains: Web & Interfaces 529, AI & Data 512, Systems & Infra 307, Knowledge & Content 63, Mobile 56, Agent Skills & Plugins 52, Other 2.
- Two edge types relate repositories, and they differ in how much they can be trusted. "stack" is EXTRACTED: IDF-weighted overlap of dependencies both repositories declare in a manifest, and each edge names the packages it was drawn from, so it can be checked and disagreed with. It answers "built the way you build things". "semantic" is INFERRED: cosine distance between embeddings, with no evidence attached beyond the number itself. It answers "probably solves the same problem". A pair scoring on both is the strongest signal that one repository is a usable starting point for the other, because the extracted edge corroborates the inferred one.
- Clusters in clusters.json are built from semantic edges only, so they inherit that provenance: they are INFERRED. Method is Louvain modularity over the thresholded semantic edges: a group is a set of repositories linked more densely to each other than to the rest of the estate. That is a stronger claim than the connected components this previously used, which chained through bridge repositories, but it is still a claim about an embedding and not about code. A large group is a set of closely related projects, not a set of duplicates.
- Stack edges exist only for the 459 repositories that declare dependencies in a manifest this pipeline reads.
- Grades cover 1518 of 1521 repositories. An absent grade means not yet audited, not a bad grade.
- Generated 2026-09-09.
